external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work through a SOAP feed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app opened by duty engineers and used to call the dispatch API and receive live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it. CORS origins and credential behavior are undocumented. WebSocket TLS, handshake authentication, and session checks after connection are undocumented.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database and can control live dispatch work.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process on the corporate network that pulls and parses the scheduling partner's XML feed, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: serve app
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and API are served from different origins. The API answers the console cross-origin; allowed origins and credential behavior are undocumented.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and job-creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: publish planned work
data_flows.description: The scheduling partner publishes tomorrow's planned work to the schedule importer through a SOAP feed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer, or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write documents
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes downloaded XML documents into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: It presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit, the schedule importer runs, and the corporate hosting and file storage are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company control plane holding the live estate, where an account can move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: It is the zone holding the live estate and is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The trust zone controlled by the scheduling partner, another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch console is an internal process because it is served by the corporate web host and used from the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The console is served by the corporate web host and duty engineers access it from the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is a browser-opened single-page JavaScript app.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API is an internal process.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly says the production control plane containing the API is not reachable from the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The API answers cross-origin requests from the console and also exposes a WebSocket endpoint.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is a batch importer that periodically pulls and parses a SOAP feed and posts work orders.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is in the production control plane.
assumptions.basis: The database is the dispatch API's backing store, and the API runs in the production control plane.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is confidential.
assumptions.basis: It contains crew mobile numbers and job-creating tokens or sessions, which are personal and security-sensitive data.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule archive contains business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It stores planned work documents used by the field dispatch platform.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate web host is internal.
assumptions.basis: The text identifies it as the corporate web host serving the internal dispatch console.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate web host presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It serves a browser-accessed JavaScript application.
